lesson.scenario: A profile update and its dependent notification are delivered using vector dependencies despite network reordering.
entities: Creates the profile update with vector component A
Observes A then creates a dependent notification
Carries both vector-stamped messages to C
Stores messages whose dependencies are missing

steps.title: A creates the cause
steps.narration: A increments its vector and publishes profile version m1 at [1,0].
steps.outcome: m1 names its own A event and has no B dependency.
steps.invariant: A increments only its own vector component before sending.

steps.title: B observes then responds
steps.narration: B delivers m1, merges [1,0], increments B, and creates notification m2 at [1,1].
steps.outcome: m2 explicitly depends on A1 through its vector.
steps.invariant: A process merges delivered dependencies before incrementing its own component.

steps.title: Dependent message arrives first
steps.narration: C receives m2 while its delivered frontier is still [0,0].
steps.outcome: C withholds the notification rather than exposing an effect before its cause.
steps.invariant: For sender B, m2 is ready only when B is next and every non-B component dependency is already delivered.

steps.title: Cause becomes deliverable
steps.narration: m1 arrives with A=1 and no unsatisfied remote dependency, so C applies it and advances to [1,0].
steps.outcome: The missing causal predecessor is now visible at C.
steps.invariant: A delivered frontier advances monotonically one sender event at a time.

steps.title: Holdback drains dependent work
steps.narration: The frontier now satisfies m2, so C applies the notification and advances B to one.
action: release m2 and advance frontier to [1,1]
steps.outcome: Network order m2,m1 becomes causal application order m1,m2.
steps.invariant: Concurrent messages may be ordered either way, but a dependency must never follow its effect.

production.scenario: An incident-bridge chat service holds replies until their parent messages are visible so war-room participants never see a response before the message it references.
components: Sends a reply to the on-call war-room thread during an outage
Owns room writes and dependency metadata for the incident room
Authoritative record of room messages, edits, and reactions
Waits until every referenced message is already visible in the room
Carries released room events to web and mobile clients after dependency checks
Render the live incident thread to responders on different devices
Replays unresolved room events after a region reconnect
flows: reply to message 812 with dependency metadata
The responder sends a reply that explicitly references the earlier message about a failing token issuer.
The chat API stores both the new payload and the list of messages that must already be visible first.
The delivery buffer reads what the room has already exposed so it can evaluate whether the reply is ready.
release reply when parent is visible
Only after message 812 is in the visible frontier does the buffer hand the reply to the room delivery stream.
Web and mobile responders see the parent message first, then the answer, even if packets arrived out of order.
replay unresolved room events after WAN recovery
When the chat region reconnects, the resync job rechecks held events against the authoritative room log before releasing them.
